Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: "measured ghost arrival = 25.6 control trades/day", used to plan the confirm n=600 sample.
findings.problem: That rate is a backfill artefact, not a measurement of the live tape: control's 1541 screen trades over the stated 61.0-day span is ~25/day, matching 25.6 almost exactly, whereas the live tier holds only 25 events in total and control's live_n is 4. The word "measured" implies live arrival; at the live rate actually observed, confirm n=600 is nowhere near reachable on the implied horizon. Every timeline claim resting on 25.6/day is resting on backfill.

findings.claim: Checklist backfill_cannot_promote = ok, "Only live-tape evidence can promote — 0 surfaced arm(s); none promoted from a screen".
findings.problem: The check is green because nothing has ever been surfaced, so the guard has never been exercised — that establishes absence of a promotion, not the existence of a working block. Meanwhile every headline number in the arena (screen_wr, screen_ev, screen_dWR up to 5.26pp on n=1540) is backfill-derived, and arms already carry the label 'confirm' while their live_n is 1-4. A green box here reads as 'backfill is contained' when the only containment demonstrated is that no arm has finished.

findings.claim: entry-8pct screen_wr=51.417 and vol-4x screen_wr=51.103, both above control's 49.903, while both report screen_dWR=0.0pp.
findings.problem: These two arms are scored on 494 and 861 events against control's 1541 on the same shared stream — they are filters, so their WR levels come from a different subpopulation and are not comparable to control's level. The loop's own methodology says to report delta on the same window and never quote a level, yet the only WR advantage visible for these arms is exactly such a level, and their paired delta is flat at 0.0pp. Reporting both side by side invites the population-mismatch read the graveyard already killed twice (G-08, G-09).

findings.claim: sl-5pct is the strongest arm, screen_dWR=+5.26pp on screen_n=1540.
findings.problem: On the same row its screen_ev is 0.022 against control's 0.029 — it is worse on EV per trade while better on win rate, and the fixed objective requires both. That is the precise signature of a win-rate dial that does not pay, which G-08 and G-17 already killed for the pump threshold. Presenting the +5.26pp as the arm's headline without the EV regression beside it misrepresents it against the stated objective.

findings.claim: Every screen_dWR in the arena (sl-5pct +5.26pp, hold-12h +3.18pp, tp-7pct -3.44pp) reported against corrected alpha = 0.00833.
findings.problem: Not one running arm reports the discordant-pair counts (b/c) or a paired p-value, so none of these deltas can actually be compared with the 0.00833 bar — the alpha is stated but unusable. The loop demonstrably can produce these: the retired L-sl-entry-anchor kill cites paired p=9.18e-41 with b=0/c=134 on n=1474. Deltas presented without the test that would gate them are decorative, and the largest one is the arm nearest promotion.

findings.claim: Checklist no_lookahead = ok, "Detection is look-ahead free — re-detected 108 events on truncated history across 6 coins; mismatches: none".
findings.problem: 108 events across 6 coins is roughly 2% of the 4789-event shared population and about 3% of the 176 coins in the dataset. A clean re-detection on that slice does not establish look-ahead freedom for the whole detection stream, particularly for the coins where the kernel is known to disagree with the live bot (4 of 5 kernel_agreement misses are BOME). Given LA is the project's first-listed failure mode and killed G-01 and G-18, the green here is broader than what the sample supports.
